lesson.title: Centered on the Truth: The Mean of the Sample Proportion
lesson.summary: The mean of the sampling distribution of p-hat is exactly equal to the population proportion p, which makes the sample proportion an unbiased estimator.
lesson.body:
Return to the marble example from the previous chapter: five marbles, two red, so p = 0.4, and the sampling distribution of p-hat for samples of size two was p-hat = 0 with probability 3/10, p-hat = 0.5 with probability 6/10, and p-hat = 1 with probability 1/10. The mean of that sampling distribution is found the same way you find the mean of any discrete distribution, by multiplying each value by its probability and summing: (0)(3/10) + (0.5)(6/10) + (1)(1/10) = 0 + 3/10 + 1/10 = 4/10 = 0.4.

That result, 0.4, is exactly equal to p, the true population proportion. This is not a coincidence of this particular example, it is a general fact: the mean of the sampling distribution of p-hat always equals p, for any population and any sample size, as long as sampling is done randomly. Statisticians write this as mu of p-hat equals p.

This connects directly back to the idea of an unbiased estimator. Because the mean of p-hat's sampling distribution equals the parameter p exactly, with no systematic overshoot or undershoot, p-hat is an unbiased estimator of p. That is a meaningful guarantee: even though any individual sample proportion will typically miss the true p by some amount, there is no built-in tendency for p-hat to run consistently high or consistently low. Averaged over all possible samples, it hits the target exactly.

It is worth restating what this guarantee does and does not promise. It does not mean a single p-hat from a single sample will equal p, in the marble example not one of the ten possible samples produced p-hat = 0.4 exactly, even though the average of all ten did. What it promises is that there is no directional bias built into the sampling process itself: the sampling distribution is centered exactly where it should be. Understanding how far individual samples might land from that center is the job of the standard deviation, taken up next.
